workflow: Git worktrees are the correct isolation unit for parallel GSD planners: each worktree gets its own git index, preventing index.lock collisions and branch-switching races between concurrent agents.

Workflow: checkout main in the main tree, then `git worktree add <path> <branch>` before launching a background planner — the agent inherits the right branch and can commit without touching the main tree.
Symlinking node_modules into a worktree is fragile; running `pnpm i` in the worktree is the correct approach for husky/lint-staged compatibility.
GSD commit helper false-negatives (reports commit_failed but commit actually landed) — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` after a GSD commit before acting on the error.

When a session/usage limit interrupts a background agent: check the worktree HEAD to see how far it got, verify no partial commits, then restart. The agent's startup `pnpm i` is idempotent so restarting is safe.

Background agents should not be launched with isolation:worktree in the Agent tool call here — worktree setup must be done manually beforehand so the agent's commits land on the right pre-existing branch.
